title: Germany – Software package and information systems – ITDZ Berlin: OV RV Datenschleuse
description: Gegenstand ist die Lieferung, Installation und Konfiguration einer umfassenden Softwarelösung auf der Hardware des Auftraggebers für den sicheren Datenaustausch und die Datensynchronisation zur eigenen Nutzung sowie zur Kundennutzung. Ein Weiterverkauf von Lizenzen ist nicht Teil dieses Rahmenvertrags. Des Weiteren ist ausschließlich der Auftraggeber einziger Ansprechpartner für Abrufe von Supportleistungen. Die Lösung soll den kontrollierten Transfer von Dateien zwischen Netzwerkbereichen, Sicherheitszonen und Standorten mit unterschiedlichem Sicherheitsgefälle ermöglichen und dabei höchste Anforderungen an IT-Sicherheit, Datenschutz und Compliance erfüllen.

title: Germany – Architectural and related services – Generalplanerleistungen für den Ausbau der Strohgäubahn zwischen Korntal und Ditzingen-Heimerdingen
description: Der Auftraggeber beabsichtigt, Generalplanerleistungen für den Ausbau der Strohgäubahn zwischen Korntal und Ditzingen-Heimerdingen zu vergeben. Der Auftragnehmer erbringt dabei zunächst als Generalplaner mit Steuerungsfunktion über alle Gewerke die Leistungsphasen 1 und 2 nach HOAI für die Leistungsbilder Verkehrsanlagen, Ingenieurbauwerke (Objekt- und Tragwerksplanung), technische Ausrüstung und Landschaftspflegerischer Begleitplan sowie die für eine Genehmigungsplanung erforderlichen Gutachten in der für die Leistungsphase 2 notwendigen Tiefe. Planungsziel ist ein wirtschaftlicher, genehmigungsfähiger Zielzustand, der mit einem Vorplanungsheft nach DB Ril 809 einschließlich abgestimmter Vorzugsvariante als Grundlage für die anschließende Nutzen-Kosten-Untersuchung abzuschließen ist. Die Leistungen werden voraussichtlich wie folgt stufenweise beauftragt: Verbindlich beauftragt wird zunächst Stufe 1 (Leistungsphasen 1 und 2 nach HOAI - Grundlagenermittlung und Vorplanung). Die Beauftragung von Stufe 2 (Leistungsphasen 3 bis 7 nach HOAI) und Stufe 3 (Leistungsphasen 8 bis 9 nach HOAI) erfolgt durch gesonderten Abruf des Auftraggebers. Ein Rechtsanspruch des Auftragnehmers auf Beauftragung der weiteren Stufen besteht nicht. Der Abruf der Folgestufen wird insbesondere unter dem Vorbehalt der Projektfortführungsentscheidungen der zuständigen Gremien sowie der Sicherstellung der Finanzierung - insbesondere der Genehmigung der Fördermittel - stehen. Die Leistungen werden mit Fördermitteln des Landes kofinanziert.

Die Leistungen beinhalten die regelmäßige Inspektion und Wartung sowie Prüfung und Sicherstellung der Funktionsfähigkeit im Bestand.

title: Ireland – Installation services of electrical and mechanical equipment – Schools Energy Pathfinder 2025 Biomass Programme Biomass Package Bundle 2 LMETB
description: Invitation to Tenders is sought from suitably qualified Contractors to undertake the complete Project Scope comprising of supply, delivery, installation and commissioning of modular off-site constructed containerised biomass cabins and the subsequent supply and delivery of fuel to each school for a period of 15 years. The successful Contractor will be required to enter into two separate contracts covering the works element Contract A and the supply of fuel element Contract B as follows: a. Contract A: Public Works Contract PWC relating to the supply, delivery, installation and commissioning of modular off-site constructed containerised biomass cabins including plantroom and equipment to each school within this Bundle. b. Contract B: Local Energy Supply Contract LESC relating to the supply and delivery of fuel wood pellets and sale of heat, including full operation, maintenance, repair and replacement of biomass cabin equipment to each school within this Bundle for a period of 15 years. The Project Scope is for five 5 school site locations 2 schools in County Louth 3 schools in County Meath.

title: VE 906 Leitstellen IT-Infrastruktur
description: Die Integrierte Leitstelle Rems-Murr (ILS) und die Integrierte Regionalleitstelle Ostwürttemberg (IRLS) werden die beiden Leitstellen zukünftig als Partnerleitstellen so betreiben, dass die Leitstellen im Regelbetrieb eng zusammenarbeiten und sich gegenseitig unterstützen. Im Falle eines Ausfalls eines Standortes sollen beide Leitstellen von einem Standort aus betrieben werden. Dazu wird entsprechende Leitstellen-IT-Infrastruktur beschafft, so dass die Leitstellen zukünftig in einem Verbund arbeiten. Die Leistung umfasst dabei für beide Standorte • das IT-Virtualisierungssystem zum Betrieb der Leitstellen-Einsatzleitsoftware COBRA des Herstellers ISE zur Notrufbearbeitung, Telekommunikation und Funk-Vermittlung und dessen Schnittstellen. • IT-Sicherheitsinfrastruktur • die dazu notwendige Netzwerkinfrastruktur, bestehend aus Netzwerken und Netzwerkmanagement, inkl. Monitoring • Integration von Verschlüsselungskomponenten • Gebäudetechnikintegration • Schnittstellen zu verschiedenen externen Systemen (RTT, AML, BMA, DA, KMS, etc.) • und die zugehörigen Projektdienstleistungen. Der Leistungsumfang des Auftragnehmers (AN) umfasst die Bereitstellung der für die jeweiligen Systeme erforderlichen Software- und Hardwarekomponenten sowie die Sicherstellung der vollständigen Funktionsfähigkeit der Schnittstellen untereinander. Der AN erbringt neben dem Aufbau der Systeme explizit auch die Leistung eines Systemintegrators. Seine Aufgabe ist die Integration des eigenen Systems und der für dieses Projekt beigestellten, über Schnittstellen verbundenen Systeme und weiterer Einrichtungen des AG. Hauptmassen: Virtualisierungsserver / Firewalls / Netzwerkkomponenten /Arbeitsplatzrechner

title: France – Repair and maintenance of plant – RENOVATION DES DEGRILLEURS/SKIP DES STATIONS DE RELEVAGE DE L'EPERVIERE ET DE CHAFFIT
description: L’aménagement hydroélectrique de Beauchastel dispose de trois stations de relevage : la station de Blaud, la station de Chaffit et la station de l’Épervière. Chacune de ces stations est équipée de pompes permettant d’assurer le relevage des eaux provenant des canaux de fuite des digues. Elles disposent également de dégrilleurs automatiques de type « râteaux », destinés à assurer le nettoyage des grilles amont et à évacuer les détritus retenus par celles-ci. Historiquement, les quatre dégrilleurs présents sur les trois stations étaient de conception similaire et de fabrication JONNERET. En 2024, deux de ces équipements ont été entièrement remplacés par des dégrilleurs neufs, leur état de dégradation ayant été jugé incompatible avec une rénovation. Dans le cadre de la remise à niveau de ses installations, CNR souhaite désormais rénover les deux dégrilleurs restants. Le périmètre des travaux comprend également la rénovation d'un équipement de levage destinés à la manutention et à l’évacuation des détritus, situé sur le site de l’Épervière. Les trois stations de relevage ont été mises en service en 1966. Compte tenu de l’ancienneté des installations, le marché comprendra des travaux de nature mécanique et électrique visant à remettre à niveau les équipements concernés, à améliorer leur fiabilité et à garantir leur pérennité. Une part de rétroconception mécanique sera également à prévoir. En effet, CNR ne dispose pas de l’ensemble des plans de détail d’origine relatifs à certains équipements. Le titulaire devra donc, lorsque nécessaire, réaliser les relevés dimensionnels et investigations permettant de reconstituer les données techniques indispensables à la conception et à la réalisation des travaux. Les travaux sont programmés en 2027 sur le site de l'Epervière, et en 2028 sur le site de Chaffit (option).

Les prestations et fournitures comprises dans le montant maximum sont les suivantes : - La fourniture et la livraison tels que détaillés dans le bordereau de prix - Les contrôles et essais de fabrication avec production des documents de contrôle et de conformité - Le stockage temporaire par le Titulaire des fournitures avant livraison sur site - Le conditionnement et le colisage - Le chargement avec l’identification des points de levage et le transport - La livraison, en un nombre minimum d’éléments, sur les sites RATP - La fourniture des documentations nécessaires à leur réception définitive sur site RATP - La garantie des fournitures - Des prestations complémentaires (sur devis) La RATP se réserve la possibilité de faire réaliser des prestations similaires par le Titulaire du marché dans les conditions énoncées à l’article R2122-7 du Code de la Commande publique. Il est à noter que le CA requis devra représenter une fois et demi le montant maximum annuel attribué.

TRM Technologies Inc. *** Financial Consumer Agency of Canada (FCAC) thanks you for your interest in our procurement process. The RFP will only be open to the fifteen (15) suppliers listed on the NPP and we will not be adding any additional suppliers to this solicitation. FCAC has met the mandatory requirements under the PSPC SBIPS SA and we are confident that we will be receiving a sufficient number of proposals to make this a truly competitive process. With our current staffing limitations, we cannot invite additional proponents without creating undo process or inefficiencies within our procurement system. FCAC thanks you again for your interest and going forward we will keep your firm in mind for our future requirements. Description of Work: The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada requires the services of an experienced, reputable, and independent third-party cybersecurity firm to conduct an enterprise-level assessment of FCAC’s cybersecurity posture. The assessment shall include an internal evaluation of FCAC’s information technology security controls using ITSG-33 Annex 3A and a harmonized threat and risk assessment methodology, supported by evidence collection, gap analysis, residual risk determination, and prioritized remediation planning. The assessment shall also include a separate National Institute of Standards and Technology Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 report to present FCAC’s cybersecurity posture in a broader, executive-level and externally consumable manner. title: PCB Transformer Replacements at Beaver Creek Institution -Minimum
description: The Correctional Service Canada (CSC) requires the removal and replacement of two transformers at Beaver Creek Institution (Minimum) prior to December 31, 2026 to comply with federal regulations established under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act and the polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) Regulations. One existing pad-mounted transformer, installed in 1975, contains polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) at a concentration of 172 ppm, which exceeds the regulatory threshold. A second pole-mounted transformer has reached the end of its service life and, due to its age, may contain PCBs. Both transformers must be removed and replaced prior to the regulatory deadline of December 31, 2026. The work includes the supply and installation of replacement transformers, disposal of PCB-contaminated equipment and associated oil in accordance with applicable regulations, coordination of electrical outages and commissioning activities, and restoration of affected areas.

title: Cap Blasting Non-Electric M7
description: NOTICE OF PROPOSED PROCUREMENT Canada has a requirement for the item detailed below: GSIN: N1375 – Demolition Materials UNSPSC: 46101600 –Ammunition Description: Cap Blasting Non-Electric M7 A requirement exists to resupply Canada with the Cap Blasting Non-Electric M7. The Cap Blasting Non-Electric M7 is required as the first step of an explosive shockwave in an explosive train when using a non-electric method of initiation. It is functioned by inserting an igniferous burning fuse into the open end and being crimped onto the burning fuse. When the flame from the burning fuse exits the end of the fuse, it ignites a primary explosive composition which in turn transfers a shockwave into the secondary explosive component in the Cap Blasting Non-Electric M7. The Cap Blasting Non-Electric M7 is primarily used in military applications for demolition purposes. Quantity: 3,000 units - Delivery to Canadian Forces Ammunition Depot (CFAD) Dundurn, Dundurn, Saskatchewan on or before 01 November 2027. 3,500 units - Delivery to Canadian Forces Ammunition Depot (CFAD) Angus, Angus, Ontario on or before 01 November 2027. 3,000 units - Delivery to Canadian Forces Ammunition Depot (CFAD) Dundurn, Dundurn, Saskatchewan between 01 September 2028 and 30 November 2028. 3,500 units - Delivery to Canadian Forces Ammunition Depot (CFAD) Angus, Angus, Ontario between 01 September 2028 and 30 November 2028. title: EW038-270870-ITQ-Storm Sewer Restoration, Northern Forestry Centre, Edmonton, AB
description: Please note that late submissions will not be considered or accepted. This is Phase One of a two-phase process. Phase One will assess interested suppliers' qualifications. The Work consists of exterior storm sewer repairs at the National Forestry Centre (NRCan), including pavement removal, excavation, erosion control, eight catch basin maintenance holes, 229 m of PVC piping, connections to existing pipes, underground power line crossings, inspection and cleaning of 220 m of existing piping, and pavement restoration. The Work also includes a raised pavement area at the gate, repainting 208 parking stalls and six accessible stalls with associated markings, mobilization, demobilization and site cleanup. The Contractor must complete the Work within 17 weeks of notification of acceptance of the offer. This is a secured facility. Contractor personnel must be escorted on site at all times by NRCan and/or Commissionaires. title: Kotiin vietävät ateriapalvelut
description: Kotiin vietävät ateriapalvelut Keski-Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialue pyytää tarjousta kotiin vietävistä ateriapalveluista seuraavien Keski-Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialueen kuntien alueella: Halsua, Kannus, Kokkola, Lestijärvi, Perho, Toholampi ja Veteli. description: Asiantuntijapalvelut rajat ylittävään lentoliikenteen hankintaan Tausta ja hankeyhteys FAIR 3 - Enabling cross-border aviation procurement on Interreg Aurora -hanke, joka toteutetaan 1.6.2026-31.12.2027. Sen yleisenä tavoitteena on kehittää yhteinen kehys, joka mahdollistaa rajat ylittävän yhteistyön alueellisten lentoliikennepalvelujen hankinnassa ja rahoittamisessa Pohjois-Ruotsissa, Suomessa ja Norjassa. FAIR 3 -hankkeessa selvitetään oikeudellisia ja hallinnollisia edellytyksiä, kerätään markkinatietoa, tunnistetaan sovellettavissa olevia eurooppalaisia käytäntöjä sekä luodaan käytännöllisiä hankinta-, kustannustenjako- ja skenaariotyökaluja kuntien, alueviranomaisten, lentoasemien ja muiden toimivaltaisten julkisten toimijoiden käyttöön.Hankittava toimeksianto auttaa ratkaisemaan tunnistetun oikeudellisen ja hallinnollisen esteen, joka johtuu siitä, ettei rajat ylittävälle alueellisten lentoliikennepalvelujen hankinnalle ole oikeudellisesti varmaa ja käytännössä sovellettavaa kehystä. Tämän sopimuksen nojalla kehitettävät kehykset ja mallit on suunniteltava kuntien, alueviranomaisten, lentoasemien ja muiden hankealueen toimivaltaisten julkisten toimijoiden käytännön käyttöön.,

title: Kameravalvontapalvelu
description: Kameravalvontapalvelu Kalajoen kaupunki kilpailuttaa kameravalvonnan kokonaispalvelun puitejärjestelynä. Hankinnan kohteena on kameravalvontajärjestelmän suunnittelu, toimitus, asennus, ylläpito ja huolto sekä tarvittavat ohjelmistot ja palvelut. Puitejärjestelyllä valitaan toimittaja, jonka kanssa solmitaan nelivuotinen puitesopimus. Olemassa olevien kohteiden lisäksi on tiedossa uusia valvonnan piiriin lisättäviä valvontakohteita. Hankinnassa noudatetaan julkisen hallinnon IT-hankintojen yleisiä sopimusehtoja 2025 (JIT 2025) sekä Henkilötietojen käsittelyn ehtoja (JYSE/JIT - Henkilötiedot 2025).,

title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Sanierung Werra Sport- und Freizeitbad in D-98646 Hildburghausen - Generalplanung nach §§ 34, 51, 55 HOAI 2021 sowie Besondere Leistungen
description: Das Werra Sport- und Freizeitbad in Hildburghausen ist seit der Errichtung und Einweihung im Jahr 2000 ein zentraler und wichtiger Bestandteil der regionalen Infrastruktur, da es eine unverzichtbare Funktion in den Bereichen Sport, Bildung, Freizeit und Gesundheit erfüllt. Im Besonderen ist hier die Funktion für die Schwimmausbildung im Rahmen des Schulschwimmens für den kompletten Landkreises Hildburghausen zu nennen. Als Ganzjahresbad mit einer Kombination aus Hallen- und Freibadbereich sichert es die Schwimmausbildung für Schulen und Vereine in der Region und dient als wichtige Trainingsstätte für den lokalen Sport. Die große Badelandschaft mit 25 m-Bahnen und Sprungturm ist essenziell für die allgemeine Fitness und das sportliche Training. Darüber hinaus ist das Bad ein beliebtes regionales Ausflugsziel und ein wichtiger sozialer Treffpunkt. Mit Attraktionen wie der 50 m-Riesenrutsche, einem Spaßbecken mit Massagedüsen und einem separaten Kinderplanschbecken bietet es einen wetterunabhängigen Anziehungspunkt für Familien und Erholungssuchende aus dem gesamten Landkreis. Ergänzt wird dieses Angebot durch eine Saunalandschaft, die den Aspekt Wellness und Gesundheitsförderung abdeckt. Zusammenfassend lässt sich sagen, dass das Werra Sport- und Freizeitbad weit über die Funktion eines einfachen Schwimmbades hinausgeht: Es steigert die Lebensqualität der Bürger und bildet eine tragende Säule der Freizeit- und Sportinfrastruktur in Hildburghausen und Süddthüringen. Während die lange diskutierte und komplexe Sanierung des Freibadbereiches im Jahr 2024 abgeschlossen werden konnte, steht nun die umfassende Ertüchtigung der Schwimmhalle selbst an. Trotz einer kleineren Sanierung der Halle im Jahr 2018 sind die technischen Anlagen, die Gebäudehülle und die Innenbereiche nach über zwei Jahrzehnten intensiver Nutzung in einem Zustand, der eine Generalüberholung notwendig macht. Diese Sanierung muss deutlich über kosmetische Reparaturen hinausgehen und die technische, energetische und gestalterische Modernisierung der gesamten Halle sowie der angeschlossenen Saunalandschaft umfassen. Ziel ist es, den Energieverbrauch langfristig zu senken und das Bad zukunftsfähig zu machen. Die Sanierung des Werra Sport- und Freizeitbades ist eine komplexe und anspruchsvolle Planungsaufgabe, für die ein kompetentes Planerteam gesucht wird. Die Brutto-Grundfläche des Gebäudes (BGF) beträgt ca. 3.600 m2. Die Wasserfläche umfasst ca. 480 m2. Für die geplante Maßnahme werden Baukosten von ca. 4,0 Mio Euro (Brutto, KG 300 und 400) veranschlagt.

Responses are tentatively set to be available that same day, November 2, 2026 on or before close of business (4:00PM AST) ______________________________________________________________________ This notice is ammended to upload project Statement of Work file titled: "SOW TUMR 272101 - Replacement of HVAC UNIT BLDG 11.Rev 1.0" --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- This notice is ammended to reflect correct due date for the receipt of offers time zone to read (AST) and to correct number of HVAC units to be replaced to read "One 10 Ton Unit" This ammendment also uploads ammended SF1449 reflecting extended due date for the receipt of offers to read "Nov 5" No other changes are either expressed or implied. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- This notice is ammended to change site visit date from October 28 to October 29, 2026 at 9:00AM EST (local time) and to change the due date for the receipt of offers from November 3 to read November 5, 2006. No other changes are either expressed or implied. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The 156th Wing, at the Muniz Air National Guard Base, Carolina, Puerto Rico intends to issue a Request for Quotes conducted under the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12 procedures for commercial services to award a single firm fixed-price contract for services, non-personal, to provide all supervision, transportation, labor, materials, equipment, fuel and any other needed materials and quality control necessary, except as specified in Paragraph 3.0 as Government Furnished items, to supply and install one 10-ton unit to replace existing piece of equipment that has failed . Currently, HVAC unit are inoperable and/or confronting problems to cycle completion due to main compressor leaks. The main purpose of this project is to provide a new unit to reach adequate temperature control in the working areas located at Bldg.11, Mu�iz Air National Guard Base, Carolina, Puerto Rico. Work shall be in accordance to instructions and specifications contained in the Statement of Works (SOW) incorporated in this solicitation. Contract completion time is 30 calendar days after receipt of contract to include inspection and punch lists. KEY SOLICITATION DETAILS: Set-Aside: 100% Small Business Set-Aside NAICS Code: 238220 - Plumbing, Heating, and Air-Conditioning Contractors Small Business Size Standard: $19M Period of Performance (PoP): 30 Days after receipt of contract SITE VISIT INFORMATION: Our agency will host a site visit on October 29, 2026, 9:00 AM AST (local time), to be held at the 156th Wing Bldg.11, Mu�iz Air National Guard Base, Carolina, Puerto Rico. Interested contractors are encouraged to attend. Although not mandatory, scheduled site visit is critical. We are trying to mitigate potential risks and damages for the government and contractor by showcasing the project level of effort. We suggest you carry all necessary material to take notes/measurements during the visit, as needed. No questions will not be answered during the visit, instead they will be answered in writing by responding to questions via requests for information (RFI), The solicitation and associated information will be available only from the Contract Opportunities page at SAM.gov. To obtain installation access, interested parties must submit a request for attendance no later than 2:00 PM EST on October 27, 2026, to angel.solis.2@us.af.mil The request for attendance must include: Firm Name and Telephone Number Visitor (s) Name Copy of valid Real ID Act compliant Driver�s License and or US Passport. IMPORTANT BASE ACCESS NOTICE: 156th Wing Mu�iz Air National Guard Base is a secure Air Force installation. Access is controlled strictly by security forces. For those processing on-site, you must bring a valid state/federal ID, current vehicle registration, and proof of vehicle insurance. Concealed carry, open carry, and personal firearms of any kind are strictly prohibited on the installation. REQUESTS FOR INFORMATION (RFIs): Requests for Information shall be submitted on or before 9:00 AM AST on November 2, 2026, to the following email address: angel.solis.2@us.af.mil . Information provided at the site visits, as well as questions, shall not change/qualify the terms and conditions of the solicitation. Any needed changes to the solicitation will be implemented via a formal amendment. Tentative date for posting our agency responses in the SAM.gov notice shall be that same day, November 2, 2026 by close of business (4:00PM). SOLICITATION DOCUMENTS: Project specifics, full instructions to offerors, and evaluation criteria can be found in the attached Standard Form (SF) 1449 Section L and associated documents. A complete bid package must contain the following: Offer, Standard Form (SF) 1449 blocks 17a. and 30 (complete all letters) Under Section B �Supplies or Services & Prices or Costs� page 3 - all items must be priced and totaled (CLIN 0001,) Items listed under Section M (List of equipment and/or types of skill sets and or disciplines needed from laborers based on solicitation Statement of Works and proposed project schedule -please use hypothetical dates) To place your quote, submit your completed SF1449 to angel.solis.2@us.af.mil . Due date for the receipt of offers/quotes is November 3, 2026 at 10:00AM EST (local time) Interested offerors must be registered in SAM. To register go to: https://www.sam.gov/portal/public/SAM/ . Instructions for registering are on the web page. The solicitation and associated information and the plans and specifications will be available only from the System of Award Management (SAM.gov) website online at https://SAM.gov/. SAM.gov is a web-based dissemination tool designed to safeguard acquisition-related information for all Federal agencies. Interested bidders/offerors must register with SAM.gov before accessing the system (there is no fee for registration). Please note that due to recent fraudulent activity, the process for fully activating (and updating) a registration at SAM has changed and now requires the submission of a notarized letter to GSA. See the following link for additional information and the latest updates to this process: https://www.gsa.gov/samupdate . SAM.gov registration requires the following information: 1) Central Contractor Registration (CCR) Marketing Partner Identification Number (MPIN), 2) UNIQUE ENTITY ID (UEI) Number and CAGE Code, 3) Telephone Number, 4) Email address. Registration instructions can be found on the SAM.gov website at https://sam.gov/content/entity-registration. For free of charge assistance for SAM.gov matters or billing contact your local Apex Accelerator by visiting their website here: https://www.federalcontractingpr.com/Contact-Us. Please note the registration for access to the secure site takes approximately 15 business days. PLAN ACCORDINGLY. Bidders/Offerors cannot log into the SAM.gov home page and search for data. Please read applicable Evaluation Criteria under clause 52.212-2 - Evaluation Factors and Section M for Award thoroughly, The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible Offeror whose quote is found to be the most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The Government intends to award without discussions. DISCLAIMER: The official plans and specifications are located on the official government webpage, and the Government is not liable for information furnished by any other source. title: Pre-Solicitation Site Visit: Leavenworth Redundant Core Project
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FCI Leavenworth � Redundant Core, Radio Tower, and Shelter Installation Request for Industry Feedback & Announcement of Pre-Solicitation Site Visit THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE only. This notice is issued solely for market research, planning, and information-gathering purposes in accordance with FAR Part 10. This is not a solicitation, and no contract will be awarded from this announcement. The Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) is seeking industry feedback on the attached Statement of Work (SOW) for the planned installation of a Redundant Core Radio System, including a 100-foot communications tower, hardened equipment shelter, and associated integration services at FCI Leavenworth, Leavenworth, Kansas. The Government intends to use the information received from industry to refine requirements, evaluate capability within the market, identify potential sources, and inform the acquisition strategy. PROJECT OVERVIEW The purpose of this project is to establish a fully interoperable Redundant Core for the BOP�s enterprise radio network. The installation at FCI Leavenworth will provide operational continuity and Core?level backup for FCC Victorville and FCC Allenwood, ensuring uninterrupted communications in the event of system failure or required maintenance at either location. Detailed technical requirements are provided in the attached SOW. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION / INDUSTRY FEEDBACK The Government requests that interested vendors review the attached SOW and provide: Comments, recommendations, or questions regarding clarity, feasibility, assumptions, and risk areas. Capability statements demonstrating experience with: Installation of P25 Phase II trunked radio systems Tower construction compliant with ANSI/TIA?222 standards Secure communications shelters and hardened infrastructure Core-level radio system integrations Feedback on schedule, phasing, and deliverables included in the SOW. Potential subcontracting opportunities (if applicable). Responses are voluntary and will not affect participation in any future solicitation. SITE VISIT ANNOUNCEMENT A site visit will be offered to all interested vendors. Interested vendors are strongly encouraged to attend this site visit. The Government may not offer an additional site visit during the formal solicitation period. Date: November 5, 2026 Time: 8:30 a.m. (local time) Location: FCI Leavenworth, Leavenworth, KS Due to security requirements, NCIC background check forms must be submitted and approved in advance for all individuals attending the site visit. Vendors are strongly encouraged to submit forms early to ensure access is granted. RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS Interested vendors should submit NCIC forms to Tanner Marshall for processing. Interested vendors should submit the following information to Kasie Redman, Contracting Officer, for market research: Company name, DUNS/UEI, CAGE code Point of contact information Business size/category under the applicable NAICS code Responses to feedback questions listed above Any additional information the vendor considers relevant Responses are requested by: Wednesday, October 28, 2026 (NCIC Forms submitted ONLY to Tanner Marshall at tmarshall@bop.gov) Thursday, November 5, 2026 (Interested Party information for market research) Responses should be submitted via email to: Kasie Redman, Contracting Officer Email: k2redman@bop.gov DISCLAIMER This Sources Sought Notice is for planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a solicitation or obligation on the part of the Government. The Government does not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with participation in this notice or the pre-solicitation site visit.

description: BIDS RECEIVED BY FAX AND EMAIL WILL BE ACCEPTED AS OFFICIAL. PARKS CANADA IS NOT CURRENTLY ACCEPTING BIDS VIA SAP ARIBA, YOU MUST SUBMIT YOUR BID VIA FAX OR EMAIL AS INDICATED IN THE SOLICITATION DOCUMENT. BIDS RECEIVED IN-PERSON OR BY COURIER WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. The only acceptable email address for responses to the bid solicitation is soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca. Bids submitted by email directly to the Contracting Authority or to any email address other than soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca will not be accepted. The only acceptable facsimile for responses to bid solicitations is 1-855-983-1808. The maximum email file size that Parks Canada is capable of receiving is 15 megabytes. The Bidder is responsible for any failure attributable to the transmission or receipt of the emailed bid due to file size. The Bidder should be cognisant of the size of the email as a whole, and not only the attachments. Please take into consideration that some attachments, when sent, may be resized during the email transfer. If the email size is too large, the Bidder should send the bid in multiple emails properly labeled with the solicitation number, project name, and indicate how many emails are included (ex. 1 of 2). Emails with links to bid documents will not be accepted. Bid documents must be sent as email attachments. REQUIREMENT Parks Canada Agency (PCA) requires the services of a Contractor for repair and improvements to the floats, connections mooring and interior systems of the Gwaii Haanas Float Camp. TWO-SUBMISSION BID This Bid shall be submitted following a “two-submission” procedure. Refer to SI03 of the Special Instructions to Bidders. CONTRACTOR SELECTION AND INDIGENOUS PARTICIPATION PLAN The Contractor should ensure provision of specific and agreed upon benefits for Indigenous People and Indigenous Businesses in the Area of the Contract. This Invitation to Tender contains bid criteria in order to provide socioeconomic benefits to Indigenous communities within the area covered by the contract. PERIOD OF CONTRACT / DELIVERY DATE Contractor must perform and complete the Work no later than October 31, 2027. ENQUIRIES All enquiries of a technical and contractual nature are to be submitted to the Contracting Authority. Enquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing and should be received no later than five (5) business days prior to the date set for solicitation closing to allow sufficient time to provide a response. Enquiries received after that time may result in an answer NOT being provided. INFORMATION National Parks Regulations require that all work is to be performed in accordance with the ordinances, laws, rules and regulations set out in the National Park Act. Bidders that consider themselves qualified to provide this Work and intend to submit bids on this project should obtain documents from the Government Electronic Tendering Service through the Government of Canada tendering service at http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. Addenda, when issued, will be available from the Government of Canada tendering service. Bidders that elect to base their bids on documents obtained from other sources do so at their own risk. Late submissions will not be considered. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Parks Canada has made every effort to provide equivalent documents in both official languages, however, if you find any discrepancies between the English and French documents, please notify the contract officer listed in this opportunity as soon as possible so that we can rectify the situation.

description: 89089 Ulm, Universität Ulm, West, Universität Ulm, Gesamtsanierung Uni West, Interne Kennung: 26-92303 Titel/Leistung: Beratungsleistung Erstellen einer Machbarkeitsstudie Gesamtsanierungsstrategie. Das Land Baden-Württemberg beabsichtigt Generalplanungsleistungen (Objektplanung, Fachplanung TGA, Laborplanung, Brandschutz- und Bauphysikalische Beratungsleistung) für die der Universität West, Albert-Einstein-Allee 37 - 47 in 89081 Ulm zu vergeben. Im Rahmen einer zuvor zu erstellenden Machbarkeitsstudie (hier Auschreibungsgegenstand) ist hierfür eine Gesamtsanierungsstrategie mit verschiedene Szenarien und Umsetzungsvarianten zu entwickeln und zu bewerten. Dabei sind insbesondere eine wirtschaftlich und organisatorisch sinnvolle Gliederung der Gesamtmaßnahme in Sanierungs- und Bauabschnitte,sowie deren zeitliche Abfolge darzustellen. Ziel ist die Erarbeitung eines schlüssigen und wirtschaftlich tragfähigen Umsetzungskonzepts für die Gesamtsanierung.

title: RRAM Support Services
description: This requirement is for Physical Distribution support services as required by the NAVSUP FLCN, Logistics Division. The services will support the Fleet Logistics Norfolk (FLCN) - Logistics Division by providing Physical Distribution to various commands, provide warehouse support services for the Mid-Atlantic Regional Maintenance Center (MARMC) Shipping/Receiving Center and Integrated Logistics Overhaul (ILO) Maintenance Support Assistance Team (MSAT) support. The FLCN Logistics Department has an ongoing requirement for contractor logistical support services, warehousing, kitting, inventory control and physical material distribution expertise. The contractor shall accomplish FLCN objectives in support of the Real-time Reutilization Asset Management (RRAM), support services to operate the MARMC Shipping/Receiving Center and ILO MSAT support.

title: FOIA - Case Management
description: This requirement is to provide all necessary contact center personnel, program management, technical support, and associated services required to host, operate, and maintain an enterprise-wide, cloud-based Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) Case Management System (the "Solution"). The Solution shall serve as the modern, long-term successor to the Department of the Navy's (DON) legacy FOIA processing platform. The Contractor must deliver a modern, secure, and intuitive capability that meets or exceeds the baseline efficiency, processing speed, and service levels of the legacy system. The primary objective is to transition the DON to a state-of-the-art, financially sustainable, and self-managed processing ecosystem. This Solution must fully enable the DON to execute its statutory obligations with the highest levels of timeliness, maximum disclosure, accountability, transparency, and inter-agency cooperation.

All sites have this instrument, and testing supplies are needed for these systems. Scope: The GeneXpert performs testing by utilizing the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) method. This is a random-access analyzer that has capacity to perform 48 assays at any given time. It is a closed, self-contained, fully integrated and automated platform capable of producing accurate results in a timely manner with minimal risk of contamination. Items should be brand name or equal. title: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation for Spent Fuel Cell Shipment(s)
description: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Center for Neutron Research (NCNR) owns and operates a 20 MW test reactor called the National Bureau of Standards Reactor (NBSR) located in Gaithersburg, Maryland. The NBSR is fueled by 30 highly enriched uranium fuel elements. During the course of a year, the NBSR produces approximately 28 spent fuel elements. To be in accordance with the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), NIST is required to transfer its spent fuel to the Department of Energy (DOE) Savannah River Site (SRS) near Aiken, South Carolina. This requirement is for one base shipment to be completed no later than December 31, 2028, with an option for a second shipment to be completed no later than December 31, 2030. See attached solicitation# 1333ND27QNB610AMD and related attachments for full details.

description: General Information This is a solicitation for non-commercial products prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR)/Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 13 as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. Naval Surface Warfare Center Indian Head Division (NSWC IHD), located in Indian Head, Maryland, intends to award a firm-fixed-price (FFP) purchase order using Simplified Acquisition Procedures for Body, Retainer, and Gasket parts. This solicitation will be competed as a total small business set-aside. Solicitation Details Quotes are being requested under Request for Quotations (RFQ) N0017426Q1120. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 332710 and the associated small business size standard is 500 employees. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through the FAR/RFO. This RFQ incorporates all provisions and clauses in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01 and the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) DPN 20260507. Technical Drawings If interested, technical drawings need to be requested by contractor prior to submission date. ITAR certification is required to be provided prior to technical drawing release. Drawing requests must be made via email to deanna.l.wilson27.civ@us.navy.mil by Friday, 23 October 2026, 10:00 AM EST. Drawings will be send via DoD Safe. Cybersecurity Compliance Requirement (CMMC Level 2): For purposes of technical acceptability, the Offeror shall submit documentation verifying a current CMMC Level 2 status�either Conditional or Final, as applicable�recorded in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS). If the Offeror does not possess a current CMMC Level 2 status in SPRS at the time of proposal submission, the Offeror will not be deemed technically acceptable. Basis for Award The Government will award a purchase order resulting from this solicitation to the responsible vendor whose quote conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The Government intends to evaluate all timely quotes received from eligible vendors on a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) basis. The Government intends to evaluate quotations and award a purchase order without discussion. Evaluation Factors: Technical: Quotes must reflect the required specifications and the exact brand specified in the Statement of Work. Price: Quotes must include all applicable costs, including shipping and handling. Questions and Clarifications Questions regarding this requirement must be submitted via email to deanna.l.wilson27.civ@us.navy.mil no later than Friday, 16 October 2026. All answers will be provided by Friday, 23 October 2026. Submission Instructions Quote packages are due by November 6th, 2026, at 10:00 AM EST. Late quotes will not be considered. Quote packages shall be sent via email to deanna.l.wilson27.civ@us.navy.mil and must contain a cover sheet that provides the following information: Official Company Name; Point of Contact (including name, email address, and phone number); and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and CAGE Code.

title: 6550--Blood Bank Reagents
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This notice does NOT constitute a request for quote (RFQ), request for proposal (RFP), or invitation for bid (IFB). No solicitation is currently available. This Sources Sought is issued solely for information and planning purposes to conduct market research and determine the availability and capability of qualified sources prior to determining the appropriate acquisition strategy. I. General Information - Agency/Office: Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), VA North Texas Health Care System (VANTHCS), 4500 S. Lancaster Rd. Dallas, TX. 75216 - Place of Performance: VA North Texas Health Care System, Pathology and Laboratory Medicine Service (P&LMS), Microbiology Laboratory, Dallas, Texas. - Anticipated NAICS: 325413 In-Vitro Diagnostic Substance Manufacturing - Anticipated PSC: 6550 In-Vitro Diagnostic Substances, Reagents, Test Kits and Sets. The Government is seeking to identify responsible vendors capable of providing Blood Bank Reagents, used to perform patient manual blood typing and serum antibody detection and identification to be used in the Transfusion Medicine Unit, Pathology and Laboratory Medicine Services at VANTHCS. II. Description of Requirement Transfusion Medicine Unit, Pathology and Laboratory Medicine Services (P&LMS) at the VA North Texas Health Care System (VANTHCS), Dallas, TX is seeking blood reagents used to perform patient manual blood typing and serum antibody detection and identification testing used for cross matching blood for transfusions. The contemplated purchase includes, at a minimum: The Contractor shall provide reagent supplies as requested by VANTHCS staff to perform blood bank manual blood typing and serum antibody detection and identification testing used for cross matching blood for transfusions. Estimated Yearly Requirements: Item # Description/Part Number* Qty Unit 1 Z401U, ALBAcyte A1 Cells 52 EA 2 Z406U, ALBAcyte A2 Cells 13 EA 3 Z411U, ALBAcyte B Cells 52 EA 4 Z4411U-1, ALBAcyte IgG Sensitized Cells (weak) 26 EA 5 Z473U, ALBAcyte Antibody ID Panel (16-cell) 7 EA 6 Z482U, ALBAcyte C3 Coated Red Blood Cells 13 EA Period of Performance: Base Year: 05/01/2027-04/30/2028 Option Year 1: 05/01/2028-04/30/2029 Option Year 2: 05/01/2029-04/30/2030 Option Year 3: 05/01/2030-04/30/2031 Option Year 4: 05/01/2031-04/30/2032 Location: The manual testing will be performed in Transfusion Medicine Unit, Pathology & Laboratory Medicine Service, VA North Texas Health Care System, 4500 S. Lancaster Rd., Dallas, TX 75216. III. Performance requirements: Performance Requirements: The following are required: Packing and Delivery: All Shipping/Freight Charges will be FOB Destination unless noted otherwise by vendor and communicated to the contracting officer prior to award. The reagents shall be delivered at the time specified when the order is placed. The Contractor will furnish appropriate containers for shipment of the reagents. Vendor must be approved by the FDA and shall provide documentation of approval. Vendor must have a defined Quality plan, and Adequate supplies available. IV. Submission Instructions Interested and capable vendors should submit an electronic capability statement and include the place of manufacture for all reagents listed in the sources sought via email in PDF or Word format by November 5, 2026, by 9:00 AM Central Standard Time. - Teresa Arzola � - Email: Teresa.arzola@va.gov � - Subject line: Sources Sought Blood Bank Reagents VA North Texas HCS � No telephone inquiries will be accepted. description: Special Notice Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source Procurement The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office 17, intends to award a Firm-Fixed price, single-award IDIQ to South Texas Blood and Tissue Center, for procurement of the following Blood and Blood Products ( X represents Ordering Periods 1-5): The Audie L. Murphy Veteran Affairs Health Care Center has a requirement for the supply and delivery of blood and blood products supporting the South Texas Veterans Health Care System (STVHCS). Contractor will furnish all personnel, labor, transportation, equipment, materials and supplies necessary to provide Human Blood and Blood Products and guidance in Clinical Pathology Procedures as specified herein for eligible VA beneficiaries of the South Texas Veterans Health Care System, Audie L. Murphy Division located at 7400 Merton Minter Blvd., San Antonio, TX 78229-4404. This notice is not to be considered a request for quotations or proposals. A contract will not be awarded based on an offer received in response to this notice; however, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, by email, to the point of contact and referencing the notice ID 36C25727Q0049, which shall be considered by the agency. Proposals or offers received will be used to determine if a comparable source is available and more advantageous to the government. If no affirmative written response is received within 21 days from the publication of this notice, a contract/order will be issued to the South Texas Blood and Tissue Center, without any further notice. The proposed contract action is for supplies for which the Government intends to negotiate with only one source. The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 41 U.S.C. § 3304(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. The proposed sole source procurement will be made by a pricing agreement with South Texas Blood and Tissue Center.

title: Replacement-in-Kind Repair of Existing Perimeter Security Fence (Ameristar Impasse Trident) Brand Name or Equal
description: The VA Boston Healthcare System is seeking a vendor for for a localized replacement-in-kind repair of the existing perimeter security fence at the Brockton VA Campus located at 940 Belmont Street, Brockton, MA 02301. The existing fence is identified in the submitted repair documents as an Ameristar Impasse Trident system and has sustained damage associated with winter snow-removal activities. The work shall restore the damaged portion to the original fence alignment, configuration, appearance, structural stability, and security function. It does not authorize a new fence line, additional fenced area, expansion, or redesign of the undamaged perimeter. Work is limited to the damaged fence section and associated posts, footings, connections, and adjacent areas necessarily disturbed during repair. The existing, undamaged fence shall remain in place and be protected. The identified benchmark product is the existing Ameristar Impasse Trident perimeter security fence. The Government intends to restore the damaged portion in kind. Offerors may quote genuine Ameristar components or an alternate manufacturer�s components only when the proposed complete installed system meets every applicable salient characteristic below and interfaces with the retained fence without a reduction in security or a change to the existing fence line.The salient characteristics are included within the Statement of Work (SOW).

title: J061--SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE - Triennial Electrical Inspection Testing and Maintenance Services Requirement - Louis A Johnson VA Medical Center 36C24527Q0039
description: SUMMARY The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 5, is issuing this Sources Sought Notice to identify vendors that are interested in and capable of providing the required services. The Louis A. Johnson VA Medical Center, located in Clarksburg, WV, requires a contractor to provide Triennial Electrical System Inspection, Testing, and Maintenance for the facility. Interested vendors should review the Statement of Work (SOW) to determine the specific services required. NCO 5 is seeking responses from firms that are interested in this procurement and possess the resources, capabilities, and qualifications necessary to perform these services. Anticipated NAICS CODE 238210, PSC CODE J061 Please submit your capabilities statement and provide responses to all questions listed below. SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE: 36C24527Q0039 1. Business name (including Unique Entity ID (SAM.gov) 2. Business type, socio-economic status (e.g., Veteran-Owned, Woman-Owned, Disadvantaged Small Business, 8(a), etc.), and 3. Person of contact (including telephone number & email address). 4. Capability statement and summary of previous experience providing these types of services for the Veterans Health Administration or other similar facilities. 5. Available contract vehicles (GSA FSS, etc.) for use by Department of VA (including applicable NAICS) 6. Brief Summary of categories of services that your company can/cannot provide. 7. Certification(s) / Licenses for meeting the local requirements to provide these services at the DC VAMC (if applicable) 8. Confirmation that your organization has the capability and expertise to meet the performance requirements while complying with applicable limitations in subcontracting by responding to the questions below with your response: a. Do you intend to self-perform this effort? b. If you are located outside the immediate area, how will you self-perform? c. Or do you intend to subcontract work under this contract? If you intend to subcontract work under this contract, how will you ensure compliance with the limitations on subcontracting? Response Instructions: Respond to this Notice 36C24527Q0039 by 11-05-2026 @ 10 AM ET. Send all responses to Billie.Pratt@va.gov Subject line on email: 36C24527Q0039 Sources Sought Notice | Company Name STATEMENT OF WORK Triennial Electrical System Inspection, Testing, and Maintenance Louis A. Johnson VA Medical Center (688) 1 Medical Center Drive Clarksburg, WV 26301 Document Number ENG-SOW-2026-ELEC-TRI-001 Revision Rev 1 Generator load bank, arc flash, and power quality scope removed (separate contracts) Date Issued May 2026 Originating Activity Engineering Service (138), LAJ VAMC Cognizant Official Contracting Office VISN 5 Network Contracting Office Anticipated Vehicle Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), Single-Award Set-Aside To be determined by Contracting Officer (SDVOSB priority per VAAR 819.7004) Period of Performance 180 calendar days from NTP, with mobilization NLT 30 days from award 1.0 GENERAL INFORMATION 1.1 Purpose The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) requires a qualified electrical testing contractor to perform the triennial inspection, testing, and preventive maintenance of the normal and Essential Electrical System (EES) distribution and support equipment at the Louis A. Johnson VA Medical Center (LAJ VAMC), Clarksburg, West Virginia. The intent of this work is to verify the integrity, reliability, and code compliance of the in-scope electrical equipment, identify and correct deficiencies, and provide the documentation required to satisfy The Joint Commission (TJC), CMS Conditions of Participation, NFPA, and VA accreditation/inspection requirements for the elements within scope. 1.2 Background LAJ VAMC is a VHA Complexity Level 2 medical center within VISN 5. The campus electrical distribution serves Type 1 Essential Electrical Systems under NFPA 99 (Life Safety, Critical, and Equipment Branches). Buildings within scope include the main hospital, Boiler Plant, building 7, Building 20, the Clinical Addition, and supporting structures. The previous comprehensive triennial electrical inspection was performed in CY 2023; this procurement covers the CY 2026 cycle for the in-scope equipment. Generator triennial preventive maintenance and 3-year load bank testing (NFPA 110-2025 §8.4.2), the arc flash risk assessment / coordination study refresh, and any campus power quality / harmonics survey are being procured under separate contract vehicles and are NOT within the scope of this SOW. 1.3 Objective Achieve and document one hundred percent (100%) compliance with all applicable codes and standards listed in Section 3.0 for the equipment categories within scope, including but not limited to NFPA 70-2023 (NEC), NFPA 70B-2023, NFPA 70E-2024, NFPA 99-2024, NFPA 101-2024, NFPA 111-2022, ANSI/NETA MTS-2023, VHA Directive 1028, and VA PG-18-10. 1.4 Definitions and Acronyms Acronym Definition AHJ Authority Having Jurisdiction ATS Automatic Transfer Switch CHENG / DCE Chief Engineer / Deputy Chief Engineer COR Contracting Officer's Representative EES Essential Electrical System (NFPA 99 Type 1) GFCI Ground-Fault Circuit Interrupter IRT Infrared Thermography LAJ VAMC Louis A. Johnson VA Medical Center, Clarksburg, WV NETA InterNational Electrical Testing Association PM Preventive Maintenance SOW Statement of Work UAN / UAC Utility Advisory Notice / Utility Advisory Committee UPS Uninterruptible Power Supply VLF Very Low Frequency (cable test method) NF 2.0 SCOPE OF WORK The Contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, NETA-certified personnel, licensed electricians, professional engineering oversight, test equipment, calibrated instrumentation, materials, transportation, lodging, per diem, and incidentals necessary to perform the triennial inspection, testing, cleaning, and minor corrective maintenance of the in-scope electrical distribution and support equipment at LAJ VAMC, in accordance with Sections 3.0 and 4.0 of this SOW. 2.1 General Scope Summary Work shall include, but is not limited to: Visual, mechanical, and electrical testing of medium-voltage (MV) and low-voltage (LV) switchgear, switchboards, panelboards, motor control centers (MCCs), distribution and unit substations, dry-type and liquid-filled transformers, busway, and feeder cables. Functional testing and exercising of all Automatic Transfer Switches (ATSs) on the Life Safety, Critical, and Equipment Branches. Protective relay testing, calibration, and trip-curve verification on all MV and selected LV electronic-trip breakers (settings verified against the existing Government-furnished coordination study; no study revision performed under this SOW). Insulation resistance, contact resistance, and primary injection testing of LV power circuit breakers; secondary injection where applicable. Ground electrode and grounding system resistance testing (3-point fall-of-potential). Energized infrared thermographic survey of all electrical equipment from service entrance through branch panelboards. Patient care space receptacle testing in accordance with NFPA 99-2024 §6.3.3.3 (line voltage, polarity, grounding integrity, retention force). UPS battery system inspection and testing in accordance with NFPA 111-2022 and IEEE 1188 (VRLA) / IEEE 450 (vented). Documentation reconciliation of in-scope equipment maintenance records, deficiency reporting, and final triennial test report package. 2.2 Out of Scope (Procured Under Separate Contracts) The following are EXCLUDED from this contract and are being procured under separate contract vehicles: Generator triennial preventive maintenance and the NFPA 110-2025 §8.4.2 three-year load bank testing of the four (4) facility emergency standby generators. Arc Flash Risk Assessment update and Short-Circuit / Time-Current Coordination Study refresh, including arc flash labeling.
